messages:
alex_support: FYI Acme pinged Support — invoice for Feb shows ~2.3M more tokens than what their dashboard shows. They want a quick explanation before finance escalates.
acme_billing_contact: Hi team, invoice token_total=12,734,892 but dashboard 'served_tokens' shows 10,432,178. We tried sampling a few request IDs in the portal — numbers don't match. Can you investigate?
alex_support: Thanks. I collected two sample request IDs they mentioned and an example batch_id. Putting them below.
alex_support: request_id: r_20250212_01a9, request_id: r_20250212_01b3, batch_id: batch-20250212-9
acme_billing_contact: also linking one request payload we replayed: `{
  "model":"redwood-2-large",
  "prompt":"<system>help</system>\nUser: summarize...",
  "max_tokens": 256
}`
devon_eng: pinging infra + ML. First guess: continuous batching + prefix/KV cache interactions can lead to two different metric surfaces. Which numbers are they comparing (dash shows served_tokens after dedupe or post-serve attribution?)
sam_ml: quick explainer: we have three distinct counters in the stack: 1) ingress_request_token_estimate — what the API records on request arrival (includes prompt tokens for each request), 2) model_generated_tokens — actual tokens produced by the model execution for a batch, 3) attributed_served_tokens — how we attribute model_generated_tokens back to individual requests for the dashboard. Historically billing used the ingress_request_token_estimate for simple per-request billing.
sam_ml: With continuous batching and prefix/KV cache: a) multiple requests with shared prefixes can be deduped at runtime (model runs fewer tokens than sum of prompts), b) KV cache hits can avoid generating prefix tokens entirely. That makes model_generated_tokens < sum(ingress_estimates). If billing sums ingress estimates but dashboard reports attributed_served_tokens (post-dedupe), invoices will be higher than dashboard. :thinking:
devon_eng: confirming — the customer's invoice > dashboard, so that matches this pattern (billing pipeline summed ingress counts). We rolled a batching optimization in Jan that dedupes prompts in the runtime but didn't update the billing aggregation.
devon_eng: repro steps for us: 1) replay sample requests under debug env with `CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=1` 2) capture `metering_event` logs from the runtime and billing pipeline 3) compare `ingress_request_token_estimate` vs `model_generated_tokens` for batch-id batch-20250212-9
ops-bot: meter-inspect tool output (sanitized) attached:
```
batch_id=batch-20250212-9
requests=8
sum_ingress_estimate=1,240,320
model_generated_tokens=920,144
attributed_served_tokens_dashboard=920,144
billing_sum_ingress=1,240,320
```

mia_finance: that's consistent with the customer's math. Difference ~320,176 tokens. Multiply by their unit rate and it's the $ they saw. We need to handle customer remediation.
alex_support: suggested immediate customer message: apologize, explain suspected root cause (batch dedupe + billing counting method), and say we're investigating and will propose remediation by EOD. I'll draft and share.
sam_ml: short-term fix options: - Option A: finance credit only the observed delta for the month for affected customer(s) (fast) - Option B: change billing aggregation to use attributed_served_tokens (correct but needs testing + audit)
sam_ml: long-term: compute billing based on post-serve attribution (divide model_generated_tokens proportionally or by attribution rules) and ensure we account for prefix cache hits (0 tokens when full prefix is cached).
devon_eng: technical plan: 1) implement meter-aggregator change in billing-prod: switch source to post-serve attribution for models that use continuous batching (feature-flagged) 2) backfill for customers in Feb with a safe-path script that recomputes billed_tokens for affected batches 3) run audit job to produce list of impacted accounts and delta amounts
mia_finance: please provide projected delta per-account so we can approve credits. For Acme we need the exact delta and a recommended credit amount.
devon_eng: I'll run the backfill probe on staging today and post the CSV with columns: account_id, invoice_token_original, invoice_token_adjusted, delta_tokens.
acme_billing_contact: thanks — appreciate quick movement. We flagged this because our FP&A noticed a huge unexplained variance and it triggered an internal review.
alex_support: drafted message to Acme (will send after confirm): "We're sorry — we found that an optimization (continuous batching + prompt dedupe) caused dashboard and invoice counters to diverge because billing still used pre-batch estimates. We're running a fix and will credit the delta for Feb. ETA 48 hours for the customer-facing reconciliation." :white_check_mark:
sam_ml: internal quick repro snippet (for devs):
```
# create 8 requests with identical prefix
for i in range(8):
  POST /v1/generate {"prompt":"<shared-prefix>..."}
# watch runtime logs: see single model run for prefix
# check billing logs: ingress token_count recorded per-request
```
devon_eng: actionable next steps: - I (devon) will run the staging backfill probe and attach CSV by EOD - sam will prepare a PR for meter-aggregator feature-flag switch - mia/finance will prepare credit for Acme once CSV is posted - alex will send the customer message after we confirm numbers
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-2025 for the billing aggregator change and linked billing-backfill-2025.
mia_finance: thanks team. If we credit, let's include a short reconciliation note on the next invoice so Acme's accounting team has a paper trail.
acme_billing_contact: perfect, thanks. Please include the batch IDs so we can cross-check.
alex_support: noted — we'll include batch IDs and CSV export. I'll update this thread after the staging run.
devon_eng: staging run complete — attaching sample rows (pasted): `acme_account, invoice_orig, invoice_adj, delta_tokens
acme-123, 12,734,892, 12,414,716, 320,176`
alex_support: sending to Acme now. Closing loop here once finance issues the credit.
mia_finance: credit issued for delta tokens; will reflect on Apr invoice.
acme_billing_contact: confirmed receipt, thanks for the transparency.
